english_translation: It started raining while we were still on the way, so we ran into the house.

dialogue.shona: Mvura yakatanga kunaya tichiri munzira saka takamhanya kupinda mumba.
dialogue.english: It started raining while we were still on the way, so we ran into the house.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Mvura [water / rain] • yakatanga [it (past) tanga] • kunaya [to / at naya] • tichiri [tichiri] • munzira [in / singular nzira] • saka [so / therefore] • takamhanya [we (past) mhanya] • kupinda [to / at pinda] • mumba [in the house / indoors]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('yakatanga')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'yakatanga' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('mumba')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'mumba'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

grammar_notes.title: Infinitive Verbs & Action Nouns with 'ku-' ('kunaya')
grammar_notes.content: Look at 'kunaya' in this sentence. Every Shona verb in its dictionary ('to do') form begins with 'ku-': for example, 'kudya' (to eat), 'kutenga' (to buy), 'kubhadhara' (to pay), 'kuona' (to see), and 'kurwa' (to fight). Because 'ku-' verbs also behave as action nouns ('eating', 'paying', 'working'), you can attach linking prefixes directly to them: 'yekubhadhara' ('for paying'), 'pakubikwa' ('in the cooking'), and 'nekuona' ('by/with seeing').
grammar_notes.rule: ku- + Verb Stem = 'to [verb] / [verb]-ing' (ku- + -tenga = kutenga, 'to buy'; ye- + kubhadhara = yekubhadhara, 'for paying')

cultural_notes.title: Sudden Afternoon Cloudbursts & Dashing Indoors ('Kumhanya Kupinda Mumba')
cultural_notes.content: Summer rains in Zimbabwe can arrive with sudden intensity while people are walking home ('tichiri munzira'), sending everyone running for the shelter of the nearest veranda or house.

active_exercises.prompt: Choose the right locative prefix: You want to say 'The keys are ON the table' ('______tafura').
active_exercises.explanation: The prefix 'pa-' means 'on / at a specific surface', so 'pa-' + 'tafura' = 'patafura' ('on the table').

active_exercises.prompt: What is the difference between 'mumba' and 'panze'?
options: 'mumba' means at school, while 'panze' means at work
'mumba' means on the roof, while 'panze' means in the kitchen
'mumba' means rural village, while 'panze' means city centre
'mumba' means inside the house, while 'panze' means outside
active_exercises.correct_answer: 'mumba' means inside the house, while 'panze' means outside
active_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' denotes 'inside' ('mumba' = inside the house), whereas 'panze' means 'outside in the yard'.

active_exercises.prompt: You meet your neighbour at 7:00 PM in the evening. Which greeting is appropriate?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Manheru' is the greeting used in the evening, paired with 'makadini henyu?' ('how are you?').
